questions.stem: Which of the following is not involved in renal autoregulation?
questions.solutionHtml:
Renal sympathetic system fibers

Renal sympathetic system fibers are not involved in the autoregulation of renal blood flow.



Guyton and Hall Textbook of Medical Physiology, 14th Edition Page no. 349.

questions.stem: Plasma clearance of urea = UV/P. What does Stands for?

options.label: A
options.text: Urea concentration in urine in mg/100ml

options.label: B
options.text: Urea concentration in urine in gm/24 hr

options.label: D
options.text: Urea concentration in plasma in mg/100ml

questions.answerText: Urea concentration in urine in mg/100ml
questions.solutionHtml:
Urea concentration in urine in mg/100ml
  • Clearance of a substance is the volume of plasma free of that substance in a given time.
  • Cl = UV/P
  • Cl – clearance
  • U – Urine concentration of the substance
  • V – Rate of urine flow
  • P – Plasma concentration of the substance
  • So, the ‘U' in the formula represents urea concentration in urine in mg/100mg.


Guyton and Hall Textbook of Medical Physiology, 14th Edition Page no: 360, 361. Costanzo Physiology- 6th Edition Page no: 255.

questions.stem: A boy presented with the intractable diarrhoea after a beach trip, stool was like rice water. The organism acts by disrupting which of the following in the interstitial epithelial cells?
questions.solutionHtml:
Zona occludens

The clinical presentation described, with intractable diarrhea and stool resembling rice water, is characteristic of cholera. Cholera is caused by infection with the bacterium Vibrio cholerae.

questions.stem: Which of the following best describes the relationship of end diastolic volume to force of contraction of the heart?
questions.solutionHtml:
Length tension relationship
  • The relationship of end-diastolic volume to force of contraction of the heart is best described by the "Length-tension relationship."
  • The Frank-Starling law of the heart is closely related to the length-tension relationship. It states that within physiological limits, the greater the volume of blood (end-diastolic volume) filling the ventricles during diastole, the more they are stretched.
  • This stretching leads to an optimal overlap of actin and myosin filaments within the cardiac muscle fibers, resulting in a stronger force of contraction during systole (ventricular contraction).

questions.stemHtml: Which of the following substance follows the given transport graph?
questions.solutionHtml:
Glucose
  • The graph represents the carrier mediated transport (facilitated diffusion) shown by glucose.
  • The graph shows that, the rate of diffusion of a substance increase with the increase in concentration gradient across the membrane till the carrier proteins are saturated, further increase in the concentration gradient will not increase the rate of diffusion.

questions.stem: Which of the following ions in the thick ascending limb of the loop of henle is responsible for the resorption of divalent ions?
questions.solutionHtml:
K+

Potassium (K+) is responsible for the resorption of divalent ions like calcium, magnesium in the thick ascending limb of the loop of henle.

questions.stem: Which of the following is involved in discriminative touch?
questions.solutionHtml:
Meissner’s corpuscles.

Meissner’s corpuscles are the rapidly adopting receptors present in the dermis of the non-hairy skin. Meissner’s corpuscles are encapsulated receptors.

These encode :

  • Point discrimination
  • Precise location
  • Tapping
  • Flutter

questions.stem: The relaxation of the intestinal segment distal to the segment with the bolus of food during peristalsis occurs by:
questions.solutionHtml:
VIP

The relaxation of the intestinal segment distal to the segment with the bolus of food during peristalsis is primarily mediated by VIP (Vasoactive Intestinal Peptide).

questions.stem: Which of the following decreases the amplitude and frequency of contraction in the rabbit intestine bathed in Dale’s solution?
questions.solutionHtml:
Adrenaline

In the rabbit intestine bathed in Dale's solution, the substance that would decrease the amplitude and frequency of contractions is Adrenaline (also known as epinephrine).
